newsitem.title: JAPAN: Nissan starts exports after Taiwan lifts car ban.
newsitem.headline: Nissan starts exports after Taiwan lifts car ban.

text.p: Nissan Motor Co Ltd said on Tuesday it would start exporting luxury sedans to Taiwan, the first major Japanese automaker to do so after Taipei lifted a 23-year ban on Japanese car imports in February.
Other Japanese carmakers said they plan to follow suit but the volume of exports, however, will likely be low as most of the companies already manufacture cars there.
Taiwan agreed in February to phase out its ban on the import of Japanese cars, which was implemented in 1974.
The agreement with Japan to reduce Taipei's import quotas is part of Taiwan's bid for membership in the World Trade Organisation (WTO).
Under the agreement, Japanese carmakers can export a total of 7,700 cars to Taiwan by the end of 1997, of which Nissan's allocation was 1,081 units, a company spokeswoman said.
Nissan said it will begin exporting the 4100 cc Infiniti Q45 in the middle of May, and hopes to sell about 100 of the cars a month.
The company has a Taiwan production and sales base, Yulong Motor Co Ltd, which manufactures six Nissan sedan and truck models. A total of 68,000 Nissan cars were sold there in 1996.
Toyota Motor Corp said it is currently selecting models to be exported to Taiwan.
The new agreement allows Toyota to export up to 1,997 cars this year, but it has not yet decided when it will start the exports, a company spokeswoman said.
"We do not expect to see an immediate jump in our exports to Taiwan as the market is fiercely competitive," she said.
In 1996, Toyota sold about 90,000 cars, including those made in the United States, in Taiwan. The company also manufactured about 79,000 cars at a local venture last year.
Honda Motor Co Ltd said it is also considering exporting cars to Taiwan and Mitsubishi Motors Corp said it is considering exporting a sport utility vehicle.
